newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- The National People's Congress (NPC), or parliament, and the Chinese People's Consultative Conference (CPPCC), an advisory body, call for further reform and opening up.
- President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng attend a tea party for the NPC and CPPCC. Ethnic unity, social stability and economic development were stressed at the party.
- Tang Shubei, vice-chairman of the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits, says conditions are not yet ripe for a resumption of stalled talks between China and Taiwan.
- President Jiang Zemin says he hopes China and Japan will view bilateral relations from a long-term and strategic perspective.
- The head office of the People's Bank of China starts rediscount business with the head offices of the four state banks.
- China eases controls on domestic manufacturers' right to conduct exports themselves.
- Anshan Trust and Investment Co buys two securities units.
- Hong Kong's Changjiang Group is to invest 895 million yuan to build a ring road in Shenyang, capital of northeastern Liaoning province.
- Yanjing Beer is to raise 560 million yuan by issuing 80 million A shares in 1997.
